title: Open Facet Joint Denervation in the Treatment of Low Back Pain
brief_summary: A single blinded RCT for adult patients with spine pain. One group had a lumbar laminectomy with denervation of the facet joint at the level decompressed. The other group had a lumbar laminectomy without facet joint denervation. Both groups had their back pain and functional limitations measured using a 10 cm visual analogue scale and the Oswestry disability index (ODI). All measures were taken before surgery and at patients' 6, 12 and 24 week follow-up clinic visit.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* aged 19 or older
* a diagnosis of spinal stenosis
* having neurogenic claudication
* complained of back pain for at least 3 months

Exclusion Criteria:

* previous surgery on their spine,
* fracture, systemic inflammatory disease,
* malignancies or an infection affecting their spine
